detail.abstract:
This study examines Competitive Intelligence (CI) by integrating Share of Voice (SoV) and sentiment benchmarking to evaluate brand visibility and consumer perception in the digital marketplace. With the rapid growth of social media, online reviews, and digital platforms, organisations are increasingly required to analyse large volumes of unstructured data to understand their competitive positioning and public sentiment.

The research adopts a mixed-methods approach, combining computational analysis with primary survey data. A Python-based dashboard was developed to extract and analyse real-time data from news and social media sources, measuring SoV, sentiment polarity, and topic clusters for selected automotive brands (Tata Motors, Mahindra, Maruti Suzuki) and smartphone brands (Apple, Samsung, Xiaomi). Additionally, a structured survey of 100 respondents was conducted to capture consumer perceptions regarding digital visibility and sentiment influence.

The findings reveal that while Share of Voice determines brand visibility, sentiment has a stronger influence on consumer decision-making. Automotive brands exhibited equal visibility but predominantly negative sentiment, indicating that high presence does not guarantee positive perception. In contrast, smartphone brands demonstrated both strong visibility and positive sentiment, resulting in better competitive positioning. Statistical analysis further confirmed that sentiment significantly impacts consumer decisions more than visibility metrics.

The study contributes to both academic and managerial domains by providing an integrated framework that combines quantitative analytics with perception-based insights. It highlights the importance of aligning visibility metrics with sentiment analysis to achieve a comprehensive understanding of brand performance. Overall, the research emphasises that effective competitive intelligence requires not only measuring how frequently brands are discussed but also understanding the emotional tone of these conversations, enabling more informed, data-driven strategic decision-making in a dynamic digital environment.

detail.abstract: The dissertation paper investigates the relationship between global economic integration on the digital marketing effectiveness and e-commerce growth in India during the period 2005 to 2025. The expansion of Internet connectivity, technological progress and increasing integration with the global market have transformed how firms promote and distribute their products and services. The study develops a micro-theoretical model within a partial equilibrium framework to analyze how firms allocate marketing resources between traditional offline channels and digital online platforms. The model incorporates key factors such as trade openness, foreign direct investments, technological adoption, digital literacy and consumer trust in online transaction that evaluate how changes in global integration influence firms marketing decisions and market outcomes. Using secondary data and comparative static analysis the paper shows greater global integration increases a relative return to digital marketing that encourages the firms to shift resources towards online channels and expanding the e-commerce activities. Evidence from sectors such as e-retail, ed-tech and e-pharmacy further illustrates a growing role of digital marketing in India’s digital economy and that also leads to gradual reduction of rural-urban digital divide. The research roadmap provides an outline of the micro-theoretical framework, sectoral analysis and policy implications discussed in the study.

title: Runtime Governance for Agentic AI: Action-Boundary Control with Trusted Provenance and Fail-Closed Execution
affiliations: SPQR Technologies Inc

detail.title: Runtime Governance for Agentic AI: Action-Boundary Control with Trusted Provenance and Fail-Closed Execution
detail.abstract: Agentic AI systems request tool actions that can modify files, send messages, launch jobs, or change workflow state. This shifts the safety problem from harmful text generation to harmful operational side effects. Prompt-level governance can shape model behavior, but it does not create an execution boundary. We introduce Aegis, a runtime governance system that treats model outputs as action proposals and mediates them through a trusted decision layer before tool execution. The model proposes; the trusted runtime decides. Aegis evaluates proposals against active policy state, resolves provenance server-side, fails closed under uncertainty, and routes selected cases through Senate-style settlement, a quorumbased non-unilateral authorization path. We evaluate Aegis on a repeated sandbox corpus spanning five run families, 42 tasks, three conditions, and ten repeats per family. Across 6,300 rows, prompt-policy conditioning produced 79 risky comparator-path leakage rows. Across 2,100 Aegis-governed rows, the system recorded zero governed mock-tool applications and zero governed risky side-effect completions. All 1,832 Aegis-attempted governed rows preserved trusted Aegis-resolved provenance, and all 1,019 Senate-settled rows had quorum and final signed tally evidence. These results do not prove general autonomous-agent safety. They support the narrower systems claim that, in this evaluated sandbox corpus, runtime action-boundary governance prevented observed risky proposals from becoming governed side effects.

title: From Ledger Control to Institutional Finality: Why Tokenised Securities Need Authoritative Market Records, Not Merely Shared Ledgers

detail.title: From Ledger Control to Institutional Finality: Why Tokenised Securities Need Authoritative Market Records, Not Merely Shared Ledgers

detail.abstract:
Tokenisation has made substantial technical progress, yet tokenised securities remain peripheral to mainstream capital markets. This paper argues that the central problem is not whether distributed ledger technology can record and process issuance, transfers, pledges or lifecycle events. It can. The harder question is whether the resulting instrument is institutionally usable: capable of being held, settled, financed, serviced, risk-managed, reconciled and relied upon by issuers, investors, dealers, custodians, central securities depositories, auditors and market authorities.

The paper develops a market-structure framework distinguishing four levels of record: technical state, operational record, authoritative market record and market utility. Technical state is what the ledger says. The operational record is what a platform or institution administers. The authoritative market record is the record that market actors can rely on for entitlement, transfer, custody, collateral and asset servicing. In legal language, this often corresponds to the legal register or account record; the broader market term is used here because capital-market adoption depends on more than formal legal validity. Market utility asks whether the instrument creates economic value at scale.

The paper introduces the concept of Institutional Finality: the condition in which a financial record is not only technically valid, but relied upon across the full capital-market chain. Institutional Finality is broader than settlement finality. Settlement finality asks when a transfer is irrevocable and unconditional. Institutional Finality asks whether the relevant record can be used without bespoke reconciliation or exceptional explanation by the institutions through which markets operate.

The paper analyses a recurring architecture in which a distributed ledger platform seeks to operate the primary digital record while an incumbent market infrastructure participates as access layer, validator, custodian, investor central securities depository or distribution channel. Such arrangements raise a record-authority problem: if the incumbent must enforce ledger state, the ledger has market-infrastructure consequences; if it need not, the ledger remains an operational record rather than the authoritative one. The paper labels the unstable form of this arrangement borrowed trust: a configuration in which the platform claims master-record status while the incumbent supplies institutional credibility without acquiring institutional control.

The paper proposes a collateral-recognition test: where an asset is pledged or locked on-ledger, will the institutions controlling transfer, custody and settlement prevent inconsistent disposition of the asset? If yes, the ledger has genuine market effect. If no, or if the answer is uncertain, the tokenised asset may be useful for workflow automation but has not achieved Institutional Finality.

The conclusion is asset-class specific. Tokenisation is most credible where it is anchored in an accountable record operator and where the authoritative record can be redesigned without disrupting established market infrastructure. Funds, loans and private credit are therefore more natural early candidates than mainstream bonds or listed equities. For mainstream securities, distributed ledger technology may add substantial value as workflow, lifecycle and collateral infrastructure, but claims to master-record status require a much stronger institutional and economic case.

title: Development and Validation of a Comprehensive Attitude Toward Artificial Intelligence in the Nursing Scale CAAN: Addressing Gaps in Existing Instruments
affiliations: Taif University, St. Dominic College of Asia, Taif University and Taif University

detail.title: Development and Validation of a Comprehensive Attitude Toward Artificial Intelligence in the Nursing Scale CAAN: Addressing Gaps in Existing Instruments
detail.abstract: Background: The application of artificial intelligence in healthcare requires a nuanced understanding of nurses’ attitudes, a construct not adequately measured by existing tools.Objective: This study aimed to develop and psychometrically evaluate the Comprehensive Attitude Toward Artificial intelligence in Nursing Scale, a multidimensional instrument covering cognitive, emotional, ethical, professional ethics, institutional, cultural, and educational dimensions.Methods: In this methodological study, data from 347 registered nurses were analyzed. Construct validity was examined using exploratory factor analysis and confirmatory factor analysis, while reliability was assessed using Cronbach’s alpha and test–retest intraclass correlation coefficient.Results: Results supported a robust seven-factor structure, which explained a point estimate of 73.9% of the total variance. The model fit indices reached the thresholds for good-to-excellent fit: χ²/df = 2.18, CFI = 0.94, and TLI = 0.93. Specifically, the Root Mean Square Error of Approximation (RMSEA) point estimate was 0.055 (90% Confidence Interval (CI) [0.049, 0.061]), and the Standardized Root Mean Square Residual (SRMR) point estimate was 0.048. The scale further demonstrated excellent internal consistency (Cronbach’s alpha point estimate = 0.94), high temporal stability Intraclass Correlation Coefficient (ICC point estimate = 0.88), and strong convergent and discriminant validity.Conclusions: The Comprehensive Attitude Toward Artificial intelligence in Nursing Scale provides a valid and reliable tool for assessing nurses’ multidimensional attitudes toward artificial intelligence, addressing important gaps in current measurement approaches. It offers researchers, educators, and administrators a practical instrument to guide interventions, curriculum development, and policy planning to support effective artificial intelligence integration into nursing practice.

title: The Shared Screen Identity Gap: Linguistic Plurality, Cultural Identity, and the Architecture of Television Subtitle Systems

detail.title: The Shared Screen Identity Gap: Linguistic Plurality, Cultural Identity, and the Architecture of Television Subtitle Systems

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest. This research was conducted independently with no external funding.

detail.abstract: Television subtitle systems worldwide share a foundational assumption inherited from mid-twentieth century broadcast architecture: one screen serves one audience with one language. This paper identifies this assumption-which we term the Shared Screen Identity Gap-as a structural failure in the architecture of shared display systems rather than a feature gap in individual applications. We present demographic evidence that the multilingual, multicultural household represents the statistical norm in large and growing global markets, particularly in the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) region, South Asian diaspora communities, and Southeast Asian contexts. We examine current subtitle system architectures across major television platforms and streaming services and demonstrate that none address per-viewer linguistic and cultural identity at the system level. We argue that this gap requires a protocol-level response-a middleware specification operating between content delivery and screen rendering-rather than application-level workarounds. We conclude by framing four research questions that motivate further investigation and identify the design principles that any viable protocol-level response must satisfy.

title:
Proprietary Trading Firms: A Strategic Economic Lever for Lesotho

Industry Analysis, Developmental Opportunities, and Policy Recommendations

detail.title:
Proprietary Trading Firms: A Strategic Economic Lever for Lesotho

Industry Analysis, Developmental Opportunities, and Policy Recommendations
detail.abstract: This paper provides a comprehensive analysis of the proprietary (prop) trading firm industry, examining its structural mechanics, global growth trajectory, and the potential it holds as an instrument of economic transformation for small, landlocked developing economies-with particular focus on the Kingdom of Lesotho. Drawing on industry data, macroeconomic indicators, and developmental literature, the paper argues that the rapid democratisation of financial markets through online prop trading platforms presents an unprecedented, lowinfrastructure opportunity for Lesotho's youth to participate in the global economy and generate foreign income. Lesotho faces a structurally fragile economy characterised by a youth unemployment rate of approximately 38.9% (African Development Bank, 2025), a poverty headcount ratio near 49.7%, and an alarming over-reliance on three increasingly vulnerable pillars: textile manufacturing under the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA), diamond mining, and remittances from South African migrant labour. The paper demonstrates that each of these sectors is in structural decline or faces systemic external shocks-including the 2025 AGOA expiry, falling diamond revenues, and contracting South African mine employment-that further constrain the country's economic prospects. Against this backdrop, the paper proposes a structured policy framework for integrating prop trading education and infrastructure into Lesotho's national economic strategy. The paper concludes that, if properly governed, prop trading can serve as a digital-era income corridor for thousands of educated but unemployed Basotho youth, with secondary benefits including skills development, financial literacy, foreign exchange inflows, and the cultivation of a domestic fintech ecosystem.

title: Physics Teachers’ Attitudes Toward Colleagues and their Relationship with Physics Teaching in Ghanaian Senior High Schools

detail.title: Physics Teachers’ Attitudes Toward Colleagues and their Relationship with Physics Teaching in Ghanaian Senior High Schools
detail.abstract: This study examined physics teachers' attitudes toward their colleagues and their relationship with physics teaching in Ghanaian senior high schools. Guided by concerns about collegiality, collaboration, and teaching quality, the study adopted a convergent mixed-methods research design. Quantitative data were collected using structured questionnaires administered to 201 physics teachers from public and private senior high schools in Ghana, while qualitative data were obtained through semi-structured interviews with 22 purposively selected teachers. Quantitative data were analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and multiple regression analysis, while qualitative data were analysed thematically using Braun and Clarke's six-phase method. The quantitative findings revealed that collegial trust, professional support, and openness to collaboration were positively and significantly associated with collaborative professional practices such as peer observation, joint planning, and mentoring. Multiple regression analysis indicated that positive peer attitudes jointly predicted perceived teaching quality, accounting for 46% of the variance, while competitive tendencies were negatively significant predictors of perceived teaching quality. Qualitative findings complemented the quantitative results by highlighting teachers' lived experiences of collegial support, rivalry, and mistrust. Teachers working in peer-supportive environments reported greater confidence, pedagogical innovation, and a greater willingness to engage in reflective practices, while competitive and mistrustful environments limited collaboration and professional growth. The study concludes that physics teachers' interpersonal attitudes play a critical role in shaping collaborative practices and perceived teaching quality in Ghanaian senior high schools. The findings underscore the need for school-level and policy-driven interventions that promote trust, collaboration, and supportive professional cultures to strengthen physics education in Ghana.

title: Leadership Traits in Public Administration: A Christian and Micronesian Perspective

detail.title: Leadership Traits in Public Administration: A Christian and Micronesian Perspective
detail.abstract: This paper examines leadership traits through the combined lenses of trait theory, Christian ethics, and rational choice models, with additional attention to the cultural and organizational realities of leadership in the Federated States of Micronesia (FSM). Drawing from biblical teaching, leadership research, and Micronesian scholarship, the paper identifies essential traits for effective leadership-integrity, emotional stability, humility, competence, and vision-and analyzes how these traits shape decision-making. The paper also explores traits that Christian leaders must avoid, including pride, greed, insecurity, and domineering behavior. To contextualize leadership within Micronesia, the paper incorporates research on Pohnpeian and FSM cultural expectations, including consensus-building, relational leadership, and the influence of close-knit communities on administrative decision-making. Finally, the Rational Actor model is used to explain how traits influence leaders' cognitive processes, especially under bounded rationality. The paper concludes that effective leadership requires both internal character formation and an understanding of the cultural environment in which leadership occurs.

detail.abstract:
Nature-based solution (NbS) projects are increasingly central to climate finance portfolios, yet design-stage carbon claims often enter funding, purchase, or certification preparation before their physical plausibility has been independently tested. Existing carbon standards and verification pathways provide essential validation, monitoring, and verification functions, but they do not fully address a prior appraisal-stage question: whether a claimed carbon outcome is biophysically plausible for the project’s actual location, vegetation system, and scale before capital is committed.

This paper presents GeoCarb™ v1.1 as an ex-ante physical plausibility screening framework for nature-based carbon claims at the design stage. The paper discloses the public rationale, high-level methodological structure, and selected validation evidence of the framework. GeoCarb™ uses minimum project-level information normally available in funding or project documents to generate a physical plausibility signal for proposed annual carbon absorption claims. It is designed as a first-pass screening layer, not as a carbon credit certification system, field MRV substitute, legal determination, or replacement for Verra, Gold Standard, or other carbon standards.

The framework was benchmarked against independent satellite-derived ecological productivity data and tested through selected field and boundary cases. The results indicate that design-stage carbon claims can be made more explicit, testable, and physically constrained before they become the basis for finance. GeoCarb™ also defines declared scope boundaries, including blue-carbon soil dynamics, avoided-deforestation baselines, and regions requiring additional calibration.

Operational calibration layers, protected correction mechanisms, acceptance thresholds, model-integration pathways, software implementations, and executable workflows are proprietary and are not disclosed in this public version. The purpose of this paper is to establish the need for proposal-stage physical plausibility screening and to present GeoCarb™ as a public-facing framework for improving the credibility of NbS carbon claims before funding, purchase, or certification preparation.

title: Political Marketing: Definitions and Theoretical Approaches
affiliations: University of Perugia

detail.title: Political Marketing: Definitions and Theoretical Approaches
detail.abstract: Political marketing has generated no single accepted definition. The literature instead offers competing labels and levels of analysis, ranging from campaign-centered accounts to broader perspectives that include governance, stakeholder relations, and democratic participation. This entry reviews those main interpretations and clarifies the distinction between political marketing, electoral marketing, and social marketing. It then contrasts reductionist definitions focused on persuasion and vote maximization with market-oriented and relational approaches that emphasize political offer, organizational behavior, and citizens’ needs. The discussion shows that political marketing is best understood as a flexible framework for analyzing and guiding political action across electoral, parliamentary, and governmental contexts.

title: The Commercialization of Culture and the New Role of the State in Cultural Diplomacy
affiliations: MGIMO University

detail.title: The Commercialization of Culture and the New Role of the State in Cultural Diplomacy
detail.abstract: The article analyzes the transformation of cultural diplomacy practices under the influence of the global spread of creative industries. It shows that over the past two decades, culture has ceased to be perceived solely as a sphere of heritage and is increasingly viewed as an economic resource and a tool for competition for the attention of a global audience. Drawing on the historical periodization proposed by G. Paschalidis, the author focuses on the contemporary fourth stage, which is defined by the economization of culture, expressed in particular in the development of the creative economy and creative industries. The author identifies three directions that characterize how the new approach to the economy is changing foreign policy practices for the promotion of culture. Based on the analysis, the author concludes that the role of the state is being redefined: from the classical model of a producer and transmitter of cultural content to the functions of a coordinator and facilitator, creating an ecosystem for the effective action of non-state actors on the international arena. The dual nature of this shift is noted, combining increased adaptability of cultural diplomacy with the dilemma of aligning strategic foreign policy goals with the commercial logic of creative production.

title: Spatial Distribution of Moroccan Forests During the Protectorate Era

detail.title: Spatial Distribution of Moroccan Forests During the Protectorate Era
detail.abstract: This paper provides an overview of the forests within the two zones under the French and Spanish protectorates. Their spatial distribution is shaped by ecological conditions, climate, and human intervention. The capacity to maintain the vegetative conditions characteristic of a healthy forest is constrained by the unregulated exploitation of woodlands, specifically the extraction of firewood and timber, and by overgrazing. Reforestation efforts in the French protectorate were concentrated primarily along the coast to supply the market with industrial timber and to stabilize sand dunes; this focus came at the expense of restocking mountainous regions, which play a more significant role in environmental preservation. Reforestation in the Spanish protectorate zone was not negligible relative to the total forest area; however, actual achievements fell well short of the targets set forth in the 1944 plan.

title: Defense Procurement and Local Wage Spillovers: Compositional Evidence from the Post-2022 U.S. Emergency Supplementals
affiliations: Bogazici University - Department of Economics

detail.title: Defense Procurement and Local Wage Spillovers: Compositional Evidence from the Post-2022 U.S. Emergency Supplementals
detail.abstract: We assess local labor market responses to the post-March 2022 U.S. emergency defense procurement supplementals using a matched 61-county panel (2021Q1–2025Q3) from BLS QCEW, linked to Census QWI for worker-flow evidence. Counties with high procurement intensity exhibit a modest rise in non-manufacturing average weekly wages: about 0.34% (or $3.40 per week) at the median treated-county intensity (TWFE β = +0.0006; Wild Cluster Bootstrap p= 0.081; permutation p= 0.001). The pattern in QWI worker-flow data is consistent with a compositional channel: new-hire earnings rise in non-manufacturing and fall in manufacturing, while stable-employee earnings change little. Because the QWI data are aggregated at the county-by-sector level, however, they cannot fully separate compositional entry from changes in occupation mix, hours, or establishment composition. The headline wage spillover survives a pre-COVID placebo, recovery-trajectory controls, Honest-DiD sensitivity analysis, intensity winsorization, sector falsification, and same-sample 2SLS estimation with two predetermined defense-industrial-base instruments. Because pre-trends are formally rejected in our 2021–2025 window, identification relies on these sensitivity checks rather than on unconditional parallel trends. We find no robust effect on manufacturing employment or wages.

title: Banks, Non-Banks and the Macroeconomy
affiliations: European Central Bank (ECB) - Directorate General Research and European Central Bank (ECB) - Directorate General Research

detail.title: Banks, Non-Banks and the Macroeconomy
detail.abstract: Are bank-and market-based funding substitutes or complements in the provision of credit? Which type of funding is more sensitive to shocks, and why? To answer these questions, we develop a quantitative general equilibrium model with heterogeneous firms, banks, and market-based financial intermediaries (non-banks). Firms optimally choose between bank loans and market-based funding, while banks and nonbanks differ in their leverage constraints and pricing behavior. Three forces-valuation effects operating through asset prices, selection effects arising from firms' funding choices, and bank market power operating through endogenous loan markups-jointly determine equilibrium outcomes. We show that market-based funding always contracts as financial conditions tighten, while bank credit is less sensitive and may respond non-monotonically, reflecting banks' ability to adjust loan markups. Consequently, bank and market-based funding may co-move positively or negatively. These results imply that the transmission of monetary and financial shocks depends in nuanced ways on the relative importance of banks and non-banks in the financial system.

title: Health 4.0 and the End of Zero-Sum Healthcare A Global Commons Architecture, with the United States as Region Zero

detail.title: Health 4.0 and the End of Zero-Sum Healthcare A Global Commons Architecture, with the United States as Region Zero

detail.abstract:
American healthcare is approaching a structural debt cliff. National health expenditure reached $5.3 trillion in 2024, or 18.0 percent of GDP, and the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) projects health spending will reach 20.3 percent of GDP by 2033. The Medicare Hospital Insurance Trust Fund is projected to be depleted in 2033. Employer-sponsored insurance covers approximately 154 million people under age 65; in 2025 the average family premium reached $26,993, with workers contributing $6,850. The status quo has no credible aggregate-bending mechanism. It shifts cost among households, employers, public programs, providers, and local governments while the total burden continues to rise.

This paper specifies a Health 4.0 financing and governance architecture for Region Zero: the United States. It is the Money Paper in The Trajectory Engineering Papers. The claim is not that a single payer, voucher, price-control instrument, or digital tool can solve American healthcare. The claim is that cost, outcome, and trust must be redesigned together. The proposed architecture is organized around a Health Commons Endowment, a visible Health Trajectory Benefit attached to the Health Principal, a five-pillar economic mechanism, a staged migration path, public-purpose governance, and a legal bridge that can operate before any constitutional amendment is ratified.

The model is separated into two accounting frames. The conservative public-scoring frame includes NHE-facing and financing flows: administrative and process waste recovery, pharmaceutical price alignment, clinical-debt disposition with adherence uplift, and endowment draw net of bridge-bond service. The comprehensive Health 4.0 system-value frame adds productivity recapture as a separate national-output dividend. Productivity is not booked as medical-cost savings. The architecture is refuted if the cost curve, outcome curve, and trust curve fail to cross their status-quo counterfactuals within stated, dated falsification gates. This paper therefore offers a falsifiable specification and capital-mobilization thesis, not a settled actuarial estimate.

detail.title: Credit Risk Shifting via Securitization: From Cardiac Arrest to Rehabilitation. An Empirical Study
detail.abstract: This paper analyze the rise, fall and rebirth of securitization as a vehicle for funding loans, and evalu-ates the various proposals aimed at restarting them on a sounder footing. The first quarter of the paper searches out the root causes of the subprime mortgage crisis, with particular emphasis on the systemic elements that turned the crisis of subprime mortgage-backed securities in the United States into a worldwide financial crisis. It explains the triggers of the crisis and gives answer what catalysts led to events gathering momentum. It highlights the period of exceptional macrostability and the global savings glut. It identifies the causes and consequences of the financial innovations that created the real estate boom and bust. The second quarter of the paper explains the role of securitization, the process of pooling illiquid assets into marketable securities, in financing mortgages and discuss primarily what has gone wrong. To facilitate the market remobilization, the paper address in the third quarter six issues that need to be resolved for securitization to return. The final fourth provides an update on what actions financial regulators, supervisors and standard-setters have taken to restore confidence in loan securitization, what lessons the rating agencies have learned, and how securitization markets have evolved after the financial crisis.

detail.abstract:
The report examines evolving trends driving the family office (FO) sector in Hong Kong. Based on a survey and interviews with industry stakeholders, including FO principals, financial institutions, and market experts, the report identifies key areas of future growth in the sector. Notably, it highlights the increasing interest in private social investments (PSIs) and enhanced risk management strategies among FOs.

Hong Kong's appeal as a premier FO destination is evident, with 91% of survey respondents already invested in the city, citing its favourable regulatory framework, free flow of capital, deep capital markets, and competitive tax regime. The report also show that FOs are planning to deepen their involvement in philanthropy and impact investing over the next few years. Philanthropic participation is projected to increase from 45% to 64%, and impact investing from 30% to 43% - levels that align with global trends. Meanwhile, FOs’ demand for risk management products and services is expected to continue to increase. Hong Kong is well-positioned to benefit from this growing interest, with its unique combination of financial expertise, international connectivity, and established charitable infrastructure.

Building on these findings, the report outlines considerations to further enhance Hong Kong's FO ecosystem, including leveraging the cross-industry support network within the Greater Bay Area, advancing the development of PSIs to enable FOs to achieve sustainable financial returns alongside meaningful environmental and social impact, and promoting talent development.

Background: Major lower limb amputation for no-option chronic limb-threatening ischaemia (CLTI) costs the Irish Health Service Executive (HSE) a median €88,820 per patient; long-term health economic and quality-adjusted survival evidence for ArtAssist SCBD is lacking.

Methods: Longitudinal cohort analysis of 428 patients with non-reconstructible CLTI managed with ArtAssist SCBD at a single tertiary centre (January 2008–June 2025). Primary endpoints were AFS, cost-effectiveness versus primary amputation, and Q-TWiST. Kaplan–Meier, multivariable Cox regression, competing-risks, and health economic modelling using contemporaneous cost data were performed.

Findings: Limb salvage was achieved in 85% (294/347 patients); binary AFS was 48%, 5-year AFS approximately 95%, and median AFS 85 months. Death accounted for 83% of all AFS failures and 5-year cumulative major amputation incidence was 8%, confirming that ArtAssist achieves durable limb preservation and that cardiovascular mortality — not amputation — is the primary hazard in this elderly, comorbid population. Male sex, hypertension, and ischaemic heart disease independently predicted worse AFS (HRs 1·70, 1·80, 1·71; all P ≤ ·012). Comorbidity burden showed a dose-response relationship (P = ·008). 90-day rental (€1,373/patient) reduced total expenditure six-fold versus primary amputation (€5·3M vs €30·8M), saving €76,449/patient. Q-TWiST yielded a gain of 3·37 QALYs per patient; ICER −€21,945/QALY confirms a dominant strategy.

Interpretation: ArtAssist SCBD achieves a six-fold reduction in costs versus primary amputation, +3·37 QALYs/patient, and an ICER of −€21,945/QALY — a dominant strategy supported by 85% limb salvage and median AFS of 85 months in the largest single-centre cohort reported. These findings support universal commissioning of ArtAssist SCBD for non-reconstructible CLTI.

detail.abstract: Shelter is the largest component of US consumer price index (CPI) inflation; therefore, the accuracy of shelter inflation is critical for the accuracy of overall CPI inflation. Nonresponse in the BLS Housing Survey, which underpins the measurement of CPI shelter inflation, has increased since 2000 and now represents roughly 40 percent of total observations. Missing rent data are currently imputed using a class-mean approach based on rent tier, potentially resulting in biased imputations, as we find that nonresponse is correlated with factors beyond rent tier. We study alternative simple imputation methods based on variables correlated with both nonresponse and rent growth, including structure type and tenure length. A simple model demonstrates that alternative methods could yield sharply different index biases. However, in practice, we find that these alternative methods yield similar shelter inflation indexes, suggesting that any index bias may be modest.

detail.abstract: We study the heterogeneous relationship between bank capital ratios, capital requirements, bank lending and loan pricing using data on portfolios and bank characteristics for a sample of large European banks in the period 2014-2025. Exploiting dynamic panel data models with parameter heterogeneity, we relate time-varying bank capital ratios and bank capital requirements to portfolio exposures and loan rates. We establish a pattern of differentiated deleveraging whereby higher capital ratios are associated with smaller portfolio sizes, but only for high-risk portfolios and banks with low leverage ratios. On the pricing side, higher capital requirements are associated with only a small increase in portfolio loan rates. The empirical evidence suggests that, once banks are adequately capitalized, capital requirements can be varied without causing substantial changes in bank loan supply and loan pricing.

detail.abstract: Some US defined contribution plans offer retirees access to an annuity or lifetime income stream as payout options from their 401(k) accounts. Nevertheless, for behavioral reasons, some retirees may hesitate to elect lifetime income streams as a drawdown vehicle. To counter this, plan sponsors could automatically allocate a portion of retirees’ 401(k) assets to annuities, now that regulatory barriers to doing so have eased. Using a lifecycle economic model, we evaluate the pros and cons of defaulting retirees’ 401(k) assets into payout annuities. We show that defaulting 20% of a retiree’s assets over a threshold into an immediate annuity enhances retirement security for most plan participants. An annuity deferred to the age of 80 is particularly beneficial to college graduates, in terms of enhancing their welfare.

detail.abstract: Using repeated cross-sectional data from 2010 to 2023, this paper documents a post-pandemic structural break in China's Mincerian returns to education, which declined to a historic low of 5.3% by 2023. Rather than simply indicating a deterioration in the value of cognitive capital, the observed compression appears consistent with a broader institutional "flight to safety" toward stable state-affiliated employment amid post-COVID labor market uncertainty and emerging white-collar restructuring pressures. Marriage remains negatively associated with women's labor market returns, although higher education appears to mitigate part of this disadvantage. In addition, the declining association between paternal educational background and earnings outcomes, alongside the relative persistence of maternal educational and political advantages, points to a possible shift from market-oriented family advantages toward institutional credentialism. Overall, the findings suggest that under conditions of heightened macroeconomic uncertainty, higher education in China may be functioning less as a direct generator of market wage premiums and more as a mechanism of institutional risk buffering and labor market sorting.

This independent research monograph introduces the Doctrine of Cognitive Intent Validation (p. 6). It addresses a growing crisis in space law: the regulation of mind-operated aerospace and orbital crafts (p. 6). Emerging brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) are merging with low-Earth orbit satellite networks (p. 7). This convergence eliminates the traditional physical buffer between human thought and mechanical action (p. 7).

Current legal frameworks, such as the Outer Space Treaty 1967 and the UK Space Industry Act 2018, cannot properly allocate liability or protect mental privacy (p. 7). Finally, the paper introduces a three-tier strict liability framework (p. 15). This model divides responsibility among the operator, device manufacturer, and network provider based on black-box forensic logs (p. 15). This framework ensures space remains safe and open while preserving universal cognitive liberty (p. 16).

detail.abstract: This paper examines the seemingly paradoxical phenomenon of politically self-destructive behavior in civil war, using Sudan's ongoing conflict (2023-present) as a primary case study. Why would an armed group seeking to rule a country systematically destroy the infrastructure that would be necessary for governance? Through an interdisciplinary framework integrating political theory, international relations scholarship, the genesis of terrorism literature, and development economics, this paper argues that what appears as self-destructive behavior in civil war may be strategically rational within a logic of attritional warfare. Drawing on Crenshaw's (2011) foundational theories of political violence, Schmid's (2004) taxonomy of terrorism causation, Michelsen's (2017) concept of political suicide, and the greed-versus-grievance framework initiated by Collier and Hoeffler (2004), the analysis demonstrates that the Rapid Support Forces' (RSF) scorched-earth campaign functions simultaneously as a military strategy, an economic model, a terrorist tactic, and a psychological weapon. The paper traces the genesis of terrorism as a political phenomenon, establishing theoretical foundations for understanding the RSF's organizational behavior, quantifies the scale of infrastructure destruction, documents demographic displacement affecting approximately 12 million internally displaced persons and over 4.2 million cross-border refugees (UNHCR, 2025), and analyzes reconstruction efforts within a governance environment characterized by entrenched corruption. By integrating economic theories of postconflict reconstruction, Hirschman's (1970) exit-voice-loyalty framework, and political economy analysis of war economies, this paper provides a comprehensive assessment of Sudan's reconstruction challenges and contributes to broader theoretical understanding of political selfdestruction and terrorism genesis in civil warfare.

detail.abstract:
The major couples therapy modalities — Gottman Method Couples Therapy, Emotionally Focused Therapy, Integrative Behavioral Couples Therapy, and their cognitive-behavioral variants — share a foundational assumption that relational distress is primarily communicational: that the couple is not hearing each other, is caught in negative interaction cycles, and has accumulated unresolved grievances that have calcified into positions. The intervention is therefore structured around improving the quality of the exchange: listening skills, de-escalation of the four horsemen, repair of past hurts through structured dialogue. This paper argues that this assumption is correct for one population and systematically wrong for another — and that the second population may represent a substantial proportion of couples presenting for treatment.

The paper draws on Barrett's Theory of Constructed Emotion, the Fear Response Gap framework (Anderson, 2021–2026), the Singularity Stack construct (Anderson, 2026), and the Haa Latseení relational transmission theory (Anderson, 2026) to specify four conditions under which the grievance that brings a couple to counseling is not the cause of their relational distress. It is the predictive model's construction of an explanation for a body budget signal whose actual source is architecturally prior to the relationship: intimate layer granularity deficit, dopamine habituation misread as abandonment, outer Dunbar architecture depletion producing relational overload, and the Singularity Stack configuration in which the relationship is carrying the entire body budget restoration load that the intimate layer's natural distributed architecture was designed to bear.

The swapping and switching mechanisms specify why grievance-resolution interventions produce temporary relief followed by recurrence: the grievance is suppressed without addressing the process generating it, and the process generates a new grievance from the same substrate. The paper develops the intervention architecture the framework implies — a specific resequencing of couples counseling that addresses body budget substrate before grievance content, delivers dopamine habituation psychoeducation before the first grievance exchange, audits outer Dunbar architecture before dyadic communication training, and builds individual granularity capacity before asking either partner to communicate what they do not yet have the vocabulary to construct.

Seven falsifiable propositions are developed. The paper concludes with a proposal for a resequenced couples counseling protocol — the Substrate-First Protocol — whose design follows directly from the framework's architectural analysis and whose predicted outcomes are specified in the propositions. The paper is the applied companion to the Singularity Stack theoretical paper (Anderson, 2026) and the couples counseling application of the framework that Suicide Is Not the Problem (Anderson, 2026) applies to the suicide prevention field: the same architectural move, the same structural critique, a different presenting complaint.

detail.abstract:
Two influential industry studies provide complementary benchmarks for dynamic factor allocation. Ilmanen et al. (2021) of AQR show that traditional factor-timing strategies often deliver limited out-of-sample gains, while Botte and Bao (2021) of Two Sigma show that latent market states can be recovered from factor-return panels but do not directly translate regime information into portfolio decisions.
This paper develops a regime-conditioned downside-aware multifactor allocation frame- work that converts latent market states into implementable portfolio weights. Focusing on a U.S. equity investment universe, we extend static Gaussian Mixture Model regime classifica- tion into a Gaussian Hidden Markov Model that captures regime persistence and transition dynamics. One-step-ahead regime probabilities are mapped into factor allocations through turnover-aware mean–variance optimization with Ledoit–Wolf covariance shrinkage. VIX and CAPE are excluded from regime identification and used only as auxiliary optimization anchors, stabilizing the reference allocation without serving as standalone return predictors.
Evaluated under a strict expanding-window walk-forward protocol from 2013–2023, the framework improves downside control and produces smoother return paths, especially during the 2020 COVID shock and the 2022 joint equity–bond drawdown. The S&P 500 achieves a higher annualized return over the same period, but with 15.06% volatility, a Sharpe ratio of 0.90, and a maximum drawdown of -23.97%. In comparison, a long-only protective specification achieves a Sharpe ratio of 1.33 with maximum drawdown of -3.64%, and a long- short specification achieves a Sharpe ratio of 1.24 with maximum drawdown of -5.78%. The results suggest that factor premia remain economically useful when latent regime information is translated into disciplined portfolio decisions.

detail.abstract:
The Fear Response Gap framework (Anderson, 2021–2026) describes the behavioral stack as organized across three valence categories — positive constructive, positive destructive, and neutral — with each category producing a characteristic DOSE neurochemical profile and circumplex position. The Haa Latseení companion paper (Anderson, 2026) identifies the High-Functioning Dyadic Deficit Profile as the most prevalent presentation of unresolved relational architecture depletion in high-functioning individuals: high outer Dunbar layer functioning coexisting with a depleted intimate layer. The present paper introduces a new construct — the Singularity Stack — that extends the High-Functioning Dyadic Deficit Profile analysis into three specific population expressions that the current clinical literature has failed to theorize adequately.

The Singularity Stack is defined as a stack configuration in which one behavioral position — most commonly the pursuit of intimate connection, or a single existing intimate relationship — generates DOSE output so intensely and so variably that it dominates the process dynamics of the entire stack. The rest of the stack — including substantial positive-constructive load — becomes process noise against the amplitude of the singularity's swings. The control chart signature is distinctive: moderate mean, extreme variability, with all major excursions keyed to the state of a single source.

The paper develops three population expressions of the Singularity Stack. The first is the Lonely Epidemic Population — the person with no current intimate target, whose DOSE architecture has reorganized around the anticipatory dopamine of intimate search, producing high arousal, variable valence, and a body budget sustained entirely by the pursuit of what it most requires. The second is the Infidelity Architecture — the person in a stable long-term relationship who cannot construct the serotonin-dominant state of secure attachment as rewarding because their intimate layer granularity is insufficient to distinguish habituation from abandonment, generating the dopamine-seeking pattern that infidelity reliably delivers and relationship stability cannot. The third is the Performance Occupation — the actor, musician, athlete, and creator whose occupational structure embeds high-frequency rejection into the primary work activity, producing a process where the occupational output itself is structured to generate special-cause signals at unpredictable intervals, interacting catastrophically with intimate layer depletion to produce cumulative allostatic load at multiplicative rather than additive rates.

The paper also examines the implication the Singularity Stack carries for the couples counseling profession — its central argument being that the standard couples counseling architecture, built on the assumption that relational distress is primarily communicational, systematically misreads the Singularity Stack as a grievance to be resolved rather than a body budget substrate problem to be restored. Eight falsifiable propositions are developed. The paper concludes with the intervention architecture the Singularity Stack analysis implies — one that redirects therapeutic attention from the relational surface to the body budget floor, and from the dyadic exchange to the outer Dunbar architecture whose depletion makes the singularity necessary in the first place.

detail.abstract: This study examines whether and how workforce heterogeneity within corporate tax departments shapes firms’ tax planning. Using employee-level data for U.S. firms from 1993 to 2024, we document a substantial increase in heterogeneity over time. In multivariate analyses, we find no robust association between overall tax department heterogeneity and firms’ tax planning. However, this result masks important differences across underlying dimensions of heterogeneity. Specifically, cognitive heterogeneity, capturing variation in education, experience, tenure, and seniority, is positively associated with tax planning, whereas demographic heterogeneity, capturing variation in gender and ethnicity, exhibits a negative association. Additional analyses suggest that cognitively heterogeneous tax departments identify more sophisticated tax planning opportunities, utilize tax-related inputs more effectively, and maintain more stable tax strategies. In contrast, demographic heterogeneity is associated with greater variability in tax outcomes. Overall, these findings highlight a trade-off between the informational benefits and coordination costs of workforce heterogeneity within corporate tax departments.

detail.title: Heavy Metal Contamination in Lualaba Province (DRC): IoT-Satellite Fusion Monitoring of Cobalt, Lead, and Copper Exposure in Artisanal Mining Communities (2019–2024)
detail.abstract: This study presents a comprehensive five-year investigation (2019–2024) into heavy metal contamination and environmental health impacts in Lualaba Province, Democratic Republic of Congo, a global epicentre of artisanal and small-scale cobalt mining. Integrating innovative Internet of Things (IoT) airborne particulate monitoring with satellite remote sensing, soil sampling, and community health data, the research offers insights into temporal and spatial pollution dynamics. The deployment of a low-cost, modular EnviroSense IoT sensor network enabled continuous, high-resolution monitoring of key pollutants including cobalt, lead, copper, and fine particulate matter demonstrating high operational reliability (94.2% uptime) at a fraction of the cost of traditional regulatory networks. Analysis reveals a significant distance-decay gradient for heavy metal concentrations, with communities within 3 km of ASM operations experiencing PM2.5 levels 3.2 times higher than background areas, and household dust cobalt concentrations averaging 312 mg/kg 156 times the WHO soil guideline. Blood lead levels in children under five in proximity to ASM zones averaged 18.4 μg/dl well above international safety thresholds highlighting urgent public health concerns. The fusion of satellite data (Sentinel-5P TROPOMI, Landsat-8/9, Sentinel-2) with ground measurements validated the spatial extent of pollution sources and facilitated accurate dispersion modeling. The findings underscore a growing environmental and health crisis driven by unregulated artisanal mining, with annual estimates attributing approximately 847 premature deaths and over 2,300 hospitalizations to PM2.5 exposure. The study emphasizes the critical need for policy interventions, including mandatory buffer zones of at least 5 km, community-based environmental monitoring, and targeted health screening programs. The low-cost IoT monitoring framework demonstrated here provides a scalable, replicable model capable of enhancing environmental accountability, empowering communities, and informing evidence-based regulation. Future directions include expanding sensor coverage, integrating real-time health data, fostering regional data-sharing initiatives, and promoting sustainable mining practices to mitigate ongoing environmental degradation and protect vulnerable populations.

detail.abstract: The Irish state operates an institutional architecture under which procedural complexity in public administration is not a failure of culture or individual conduct, but a rational equilibrium produced by the asymmetric payoff structure on procedural addition versus procedural removal under the formal rules of the Civil Service Performance Management and Development System and the Comptroller and Auditor General audit framework. Adding an approval layer is costless to the adder — the delay it generates falls on citizens and downstream officials — and is rewarded by political cover and audit-trail accumulation. Removing an approval layer is costly to the remover, personally exposure if anything subsequently fails, and is not rewarded by any assessed outcome in the existing performance framework. The collective outcome is policy congestion of an estimated 1.45 to 2.15 billion euros of annual waste, four-to-six-week processing times against international comparator minutes, and seventeen to twenty-five hours weekly per civil servant consumed by procedural overhead. The paper diagnoses the mechanism, traces it across four sources (multiple approval layers, jurisdictional overlap, outdated process requirements, lack of decision authority), examines four international comparators (Estonia, Singapore, Denmark, Netherlands), each deploying a Specific architectural primitive against one source, and proposes a five-pillar reform framework (Decision Authority Matrix, Jurisdictional Clarity Framework, Digital Process Automation, Process Simplification, Performance Accountability) that engages the asymmetric-payoff structure at the rule-set level. The reform programme operates jointly with the three-instrument programme proposed in the Departmental Confrontation and the Coordination Failure (Conneely, 2026) through three intersecting reforms: the principal whose payoff function is aligned with the outcome, the individual reward function under the CSPMDS, and the Programme Accountability Ledger as cross-pathology supporting architecture. The two papers together constitute a complete diagnosis of the Irish public administration's asymmetric-payoff structure and a coherent reform architecture calibrated to alter it on both the cross-sectional and longitudinal axes.

detail.abstract: Existing estimates of AI-induced productivity gains span an order of magnitude. Random- ized controlled trials (RCTs) report speedups of 1.3–2.2× on contained professional tasks. The Anthropic Economic Index (AEI), based on conversation telemetry, reports a median of approximately 9× across the O*NET task universe. We propose a hybrid measurement that pairs AEI’s directly observed with-AI conversation time with externally measured human- only baselines from time-motion studies, RCTs, and government productivity benchmarks. Across a final sample of 25 anchors, the C∗-weighted BEA value-added economy speedup is 3.09× (95 percent CI [2.40, 4.27]), robust across alternative aggregations (range 2.91–3.49×). The method avoids reliance on AEI’s annotation-derived without-AI estimate, whose bias is unknown, while extending the RCT literature to a broader task population. Anchor selection uses bidirectional search and independent blind audits of task ambiguity and source-AEI unit alignment; sources are independently verified and anchors with documented unit mismatches are dropped. The paper makes four contributions. First, the headline 3.09× is a measure- ment of economy-wide AI productivity that does not rely on AEI’s without-AI estimate. Second, it provides an independent estimate of the per-task speedup parameter s used in economy-wide productivity frameworks; current calibrations anchored to observed deployment gains (Verschuere and Cameron 2026, s = 1.38) are materially below the anchor-based estimate, suggesting downstream productivity projections may be conservative. Third, we observe that the speedup gradient by C∗ visible in AEI’s universe medians is not reproduced in our anchor sample; whether this reflects sample composition, AEI artifact, or a genuinely smaller gradient than theory predicts cannot be settled with 25 anchors and warrants further work. Fourth, the anchor method provides a framework for validating AEI’s reported per-task speedups, yielding class-specific bias factors of 0.28–0.85 at the universe level and 0.44–0.58 controlling for task selection.

title: Mental Health and the Economics of Education in Colombia: Fiscal, Institutional, and Equity Implications of Law 2460 of 2025
affiliations: Universidad de las Américas y El Caribe UNAC and University of the Americas and the Caribbean – CLIIC

detail.title: Mental Health and the Economics of Education in Colombia: Fiscal, Institutional, and Equity Implications of Law 2460 of 2025
detail.abstract:
This article analyzes the interaction between Law 2460 of 2025, which reforms Law 1616 of 2013 on mental health, and the economics of education in Colombia. In order to understand how the new legislation impacts the education system, an examination of its repercussions in the pedagogical, budgetary and fiscal sustainability has been carried out through three complementary analytical exercises. To give empirical support to this assessment, the study is supported by the emotional education workshop of the 'Flexible Educational Model Pensar', aimed at teachers and implemented with the endorsement of the Departmental Education Secretariat of Quindío in the municipalities of La Tebaida, Montenegro and Calarcá.

At first glance, the results show great progress. The law commits schools to integrate emotional education and mental health care into their day-to-day lives, not as just another option. But when the Law is put into practice, a question arises that the law leaves unanswered: where does the money come from to pay for it? In the absence of funding, what in theory is progress becomes a burden that many institutions feel unable to take care of.

This is not to deny the value of integrating mental health into the formal curriculum. This in itself constitutes an important structural change. The problem is that a well-intentioned law can remain on paper if it does not consider the differences that exist between a school in Bogotá and one located in a remote municipality of the country. Economic and institutional capacity is not the same everywhere, and this territorial inequality is, perhaps, the Achilles' heel of all regulation.

To give an overview of these tensions and to deal with the problem from different angles, the analysis resorts to several theoretical frameworks. On the one hand, it is based on the theory of human capital, which ranges from the foundational studies of Schultz (1961) and Becker (1964) to what Heckman (2006) contributed. On the other hand, there is the economics of educational externalities along the lines of McMahon (2009). And to all this is added the impact evaluation models of Levin and McEwan (2001). It is this amalgam of perspectives that allows us to arrive at a rigorous diagnosis.

detail.abstract: Clinical large language model (LLM) agents are entering production hospital deployments, where they read longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs), retrieve evidence from clinical knowledge bases, and assist with summarization, dosing, triage, and guideline-based decisions. The same architectural patterns that make these agents useful-instruction-following on retrieved text, tool use over patient data, and multi-turn conversation-also expose them to prompt injection attacks across heterogeneous input channels. This paper makes four contributions: (i) a structured survey of prompt injection in medical LLMs, including the MPIB benchmark, the JAMA Network Open simulation study, oncology vision-language attacks, and the broader prompt-injection literature; (ii) a threat model for EHR-accessing agents organized around five injection channels, four attacker objectives, and three cross-tenant risks, with explicit mapping to defense layers; (iii) EHR-Agent-PI, a benchmark specification extending MPIB and BIPIA along agentic, cross-channel, and outcome-aware dimensions, with specified scenarios, attack rules, disambiguated evaluation metrics (ASR, CHER, PER, TMR, FPR-H), per-cell instance counts, a reference judge prompt, a synthetic-data schema, a documented cost model, and a responsible-release plan compatible with HIPAA and GDPR constraints; and (iv) a layered six-layer defense architecture for clinical deployments, with explicit layerinteraction analysis. Empirical instantiation of EHR-Agent-PI is described as planned future work, with a small-scale pilot outlined in Section 8.5.

title: Energy Becomes Flow Through Gradient: Physical Evidence That Gradient Collapse Precedes Flow Breakdown, with 690-Month Verification
affiliations: and

detail.title: Energy Becomes Flow Through Gradient: Physical Evidence That Gradient Collapse Precedes Flow Breakdown, with 690-Month Verification

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The corresponding author is the principal developer of the gradient-based flow diagnostic framework presented in this paper. The authors declare no competing financial or institutional interests beyond the intellectual ownership of the framework described herein. No external funding was received in connection with this work.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study involves no human or animal subjects. The research is based on theoretical physical principles (Onsager 1931, Poiseuille's law) and publicly available macroeconomic time-series data from official sources (Bank of Korea ECOS, Federal Reserve Economic Data). No ethics approval was required.
declarations.funderStatement: This work was conducted without external funding.

detail.abstract: In all flow systems, flux is a function of gradient (Onsager, 1931 [2]). When the gradient vanishes, flow cannot exist. This thermodynamic principle applies to every system in which a mediator flows through a tube network-from blood vessels to financial pathways. Existing early-warning systems, however, depend solely on the absolute value of flow, and therefore detect collapse only after the gradient has already died. Scheffer et al. [1] discovered statistical early-warning signals (critical slowing down) near critical transitions, but did not provide a physical explanation for why these signals appear. This paper addresses that unresolved question. The gradient is the existence condition of flow (Onsager, 1931 [2]). When the gradient vanishes, flow cannot exist. Therefore, gradient collapse is not a signal correlated with flow breakdown-it is the necessary antecedent stage of flow breakdown. The critical slowing down observed by Scheffer is the statistical shadow of this gradient collapse. This paper formalizes the principle explicitly and verifies its precedence empirically using 690 months of economic time-series data. In the verification, gradient indicators led absolute-value indicators by an average of six months in three endogenous crises (the Korean IMF crisis of 1997, the Korean Card Crisis of 2003, and the Global Financial Crisis of 2008). For an exogenous shock (COVID-19, 2020), the lead time was zero months, in agreement with theoretical prediction. These results suggest that gradient collapse is not a mere statistical phenomenon but a physically grounded, scalable principle governing flow breakdown.

title: Testing Times: Reputation for Debt Discipline
affiliations: University of Toronto - Department of Economics

detail.title: Testing Times: Reputation for Debt Discipline
detail.abstract: How do countries build a reputation for debt discipline? I develop a continuoustime model in which an impatient government, whose income follows a jumpdiffusion process, finances consumption by issuing long-term debt to patient investors. The opportunistic government cannot commit to future debt policies and builds reputation by mimicking a commitment type that maintains a stable debtto-income ratio. I characterize a Markov perfect equilibrium in closed form. Reputation building is necessarily slow and confined to "testing times," episodes of large negative shocks during which debt reduction becomes a credible signal of commitment. Reputation building is path-dependent and risky: a single large shock builds reputation faster than a sequence of smaller ones, yet it also raises the risk of reputation loss. Because reputation is built through disciplined debt management rather than timely repayment, its loss need not trigger immediate default; instead, it shifts bondholders' expectations about future debt policy, generating divergent paths for countries that maintain reputation and those that lose it. With positive reputation, debt prices decouple from current debt ratios and are driven primarily by the history of past "tests." Without reputation, bondholders anticipate continuous issuance and dilution, so debt prices become sensitive to-and decreasing in-current debt ratios.

title: Assessing the Empirical Evidence for Loss of Control from Agentic General-Purpose AI
affiliations: Future of Life Institute, Future of Life Institute, Cambridge, Future of Life Institute,  and RAND Corporation

detail.title: Assessing the Empirical Evidence for Loss of Control from Agentic General-Purpose AI
detail.abstract: Theoretical literature warns that advanced generalist agentic systems might pursue instrumental goals that are misaligned with human preferences, thus posing risks of irreversible loss of human control. The EU's Code of Practice for General-Purpose AI lists loss of control as a systemic risk that must be assessed, yet no systematic evaluation of the empirical evidence for this risk exists. This study fills that gap. We evaluate 19 recent empirical studies across eight properties identified from threat models (such as strategic deception, situational awareness, and autonomous replication), assessing the quality of evidence across three dimensions: construct validity, content validity, and external validity. Our central finding is that the current body of evidence supports a judgment of loss of control as "weakly plausible." In our framework, 'plausibility' denotes the strength and direction of available evidence, not a probability estimate. Emerging evidence exists across multiple properties, but no study achieves validity thresholds required for a stronger judgment. Validity gaps, particularly in external validity, are widespread. Therefore, our findings highlight the need for more rigorous evaluations of agentic general-purpose AI systems. However, for the most dangerous properties, high external validity may be structurally unachievable under responsible research practices, reflecting a ceiling on feasible evidence rather than absence of the capability. Furthermore, as AI capabilities advance rapidly, empirical assessments may systematically lag behind the capability frontier. Our framework provides a structured baseline for ongoing monitoring as capabilities advance.

title: The Effect of Inventory Management on a Firm’s Profit (A Study of Amo Byng Nigeria Limited, Aba Branch, Abia State)

detail.title: The Effect of Inventory Management on a Firm’s Profit (A Study of Amo Byng Nigeria Limited, Aba Branch, Abia State)
detail.abstract: The study examined the effect of inventory management and control on the profit and productivity of manufacturing firms in Nigeria using Amo-Byng Nigeria limited, Aba branch as a case study. A descriptive research design was adopted. The primary data were obtained through the administration of questionnaires and oral interviews were equally conducted. The constructed questionnaires were administered to the workers in various departments such as: accounts, production, stores, purchasing, distribution and human resources. The statistical tool used for this work is Chi-square(x2) and the data gotten were carefully analyzed with the aid of simple percentages. Based on the analysis, it was discovered that in Amo Byng Nigeria limited, there is a significant relationship between inventory control and profitability, there is an effect of inventory management on profit and there is a significant relationship between inventory control and productivity. It is therefore recommended that the firm should adhere to existing policies concerning inventories which will help them to know what amount of inventory to order at a particular time, when should an order be placed and how much safety stock should be kept. It should ensure that the management and control of inventories is effective and efficient through regular training of its workers in the inventory unit, efforts should be geared towards buying quality materials to avert an incessant breakdown of machines which may result to stoppage in production.

title: Are Natural Catastrophes and Social Shocks Usable Triggers for Economic Cat Bonds? A Machine Learning Assessment
affiliations: and Universidad Europea de Madrid

detail.title: Are Natural Catastrophes and Social Shocks Usable Triggers for Economic Cat Bonds? A Machine Learning Assessment
detail.abstract: This study evaluates whether environmental and social variables can serve as effective triggers for economic crisis-linked catastrophe bonds using machine learning techniques. We analyze monthly stock market data from four diverse economies-Spain (IBEX 35), the United States (S&P 500), Brazil (Bovespa), and Japan (Nikkei 225)-spanning 1985-2023 (1993-2023 for Spain and Brazil due to index data availability). Employing both XGBoost (gradient boosting) and LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory) neural networks with 5-fold time series cross-validation, we assess regression (return prediction) and classification (crisis detection) tasks. Our findings reveal that environmental variables (temperature, precipitation, CO 2 emissions) and social indicators (disaster-affected population) consistently rank among the least important predictors across all countries, with average SHAP importance ranks of 12-17 out of 17 features. Market-derived volatility measures and traditional macroeconomic variables dominate feature importance in both model architectures. While regression models show limited predictive power (XGBoost average R 2 :-0.17; LSTM average R 2 :-0.18), classification models achieve promising results for crisis detection, with AUC values between 0.82 and 0.91. These results suggest that economic CAT bonds would be better served by volatility-based or macroeconomic triggers rather than environmental or social indicators measured at national aggregate levels.

title: Severity - A Proposed Disclosure Metric for the Gap Between Modeled and Realized Tail Risk in Regulated Institutions

detail.title: Severity - A Proposed Disclosure Metric for the Gap Between Modeled and Realized Tail Risk in Regulated Institutions
detail.abstract:
Across more than two decades of correlated stress events involving multi-strategy hedge funds, statistical-arbitrage portfolios, volatility-targeting mandates, and liability-driven hedging programs, a consistent feature has been the divergence between model-based tail-risk estimates and realized losses during the stress window itself. In the author’s view, what successive episodes have made visible as position crowding is more accurately understood as the surface expression of a deeper convergence in signal calibration, hedging frameworks, and liquidity management across the broader multi-strategy ecosystem — a convergence that has grown larger and less directly observable as the underlying frameworks have become more sophisticated and more uniformly adopted.

The Basel market-risk framework requires institutions employing internal models to compute and archive daily Value-at-Risk predictions — and, under the Fundamental Review of the Trading Book, Expected Shortfall predictions — alongside realized profit-and-loss outcomes. This archive, maintained continuously since the 1996 Market Risk Amendment, contains a complete institutional record of the gap between what model-based tail-risk estimates predicted and what realized market conditions delivered. The historical content of this archive is, in effect, the empirical record of the convergence described above. It has been used for supervisory backtesting and capital adjustment but has not been organized into a publicly comparable disclosure of model performance under stress.

This paper proposes a supplementary disclosure metric, termed Severity, computed directly from the existing backtesting archive. Severity is defined as the divergence between predicted tail loss and realized loss during stress windows, reported in two complementary forms: an average form over a defined stress sample, and a top-N form analogous to maximum-drawdown reporting in fund performance disclosure. The proposal requires no new data collection, no new computational infrastructure, and no methodological commitment regarding any replacement framework. It re-purposes existing supervisory data into a comparable, auditable, third-party-reproducible disclosure that allocators, regulators, counterparties, and risk-committee members could use to size exposures with explicit visibility into the historical limitations of the frameworks governing institutional leverage.

The paper situates the proposal within the existing Basel and U.S. regulatory architecture, discusses the supervisory discretion that currently mutes the regulatory expression of the historical record while preserving the underlying data, defines the metric formally in both average and top-N forms, specifies stress-sample conventions, presents an empirical motivation drawn from the recurring pattern of correlated stress events across the past four decades, addresses anticipated implementation objections including those that arise from model substitution and disclosure gaming, and discusses limitations and open questions for further empirical work.

title: Hold-Out: The Injustice of Delaying Justice

detail.title: Hold-Out: The Injustice of Delaying Justice

detail.abstract: This article examines the role of hold-out in standard essential patent (SEP) licensing negotiations and its implications for fair, reasonable, and non-discriminatory (FRAND) licensing. It argues that hold-out is not merely a theoretical concern but a recurring market practice through which implementers delay or resist taking SEP licenses to obtain commercial leverage and reduce royalty payments. The article analyzes how the availability of injunctive relief influences negotiation incentives and explains why arbitration, despite offering a neutral and efficient mechanism to resolve FRAND disputes, is often rejected by unwilling licensees unless injunctions are a realistic possibility. Using the recent Transsion dispute as a case study, the article illustrates how procedural delays and litigation strategies may be used to postpone the conclusion of a license agreement even where FRAND-compliant offers have been made. The article concludes that the availability of injunctions remains critical to discouraging holdout, promoting timely dispute resolution, and preserving incentives for continued participation in standards-based innovation.

title: An Oligopoly Analysis of the Telecommunications Industry in Oman: Market Structure, Competition, and Consumer Demand
affiliations: Sultan Qaboos University and Sultan Qaboos University

detail.title: An Oligopoly Analysis of the Telecommunications Industry in Oman: Market Structure, Competition, and Consumer Demand
detail.abstract: This paper analyzes the telecommunications industry in Oman through the lens of oligopoly theory, examining market structure, firm behavior, consumer demand, and policy implications. Using secondary data from Omantel, Ooredoo Oman, and Vodafone Oman, alongside reports from the Telecommunications Regulatory Authority and international organizations, the study applies concentration ratios, Bertrand and Cournot oligopoly models, and elasticity analysis. The calculated CR3 ratio of 100% confirms a highly concentrated oligopoly characterized by significant barriers to entry and strong strategic interdependence among dominant firms. Demand is found to be relatively price inelastic for essential telecommunications services, while premium service segments exhibit greater income elasticity among higher-income consumers. Competition is driven primarily by service differentiation, network quality, and technological innovation rather than price alone. The study recommends policies including infrastructure sharing, promotion of Mobile Virtual Network Operators (MVNOs), and targeted price regulation for essential services to improve market efficiency, consumer welfare, and digital inclusion in Oman.

title: Survive, Heal or Die? Zombie Firms and Tax Planning
